destination.name: Alpine National Park
destination.tagline: Victoria's largest national park, with its highest peak and the Bogong High Plains
destination.description: Alpine National Park covers 6,474 km2 and is the Victorian continuation of Kosciuszko National Park. It holds Victoria's highest point, Mount Bogong at 1,986 m, along with Mount Feathertop (1,922 m), Mount Hotham (1,862 m) and the sub-alpine woodland and grassland of the Bogong High Plains. The 650 km Australian Alps Walking Track, from Walhalla to near Canberra, crosses it. The park protects threatened species including the spotted tree frog, smoky mouse and mountain pygmy possum.
whyVisit: Hike the Australian Alps Walking Track

goodToKnow.title: Winter means skis
goodToKnow.detail: In winter much of the park is snow-covered and only accessible on skis.

goodToKnow.title: No towns inside
goodToKnow.detail: There are no towns in the park. Stay at Mount Hotham or Falls Creek, or in the towns around it.

goodToKnow.title: Unsealed road to falls
goodToKnow.detail: The road to Paradise Falls needs 11 km of unsealed driving. Spring or early summer is the best time to see it.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Walk and ride in {months}, when the alpine air is cool. Winter snow means skis.

notes: Summer months from the park's reputation for bushwalking and mountain biking. Ski season (roughly June to September) has unsourced months, so no seasonalTags. Wildflowers were in the researcher's experiences but not in a sourced fact, so the fourth reason uses the sourced Paradise Falls.
